category_title: High-academic kindergartner with ASD who uses classroom scripts for social interaction
scenario_title: Transitioning to an unchallenging math worksheet
minimal_context: Jasmine is sitting at a round table with a peer and a paraprofessional to complete a math worksheet where she needs to color objects in groups of four.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time to complete your math worksheet. Please color the objects on the page in groups of four.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Let’s do some colors! What color is the apple? What color is the boy? What color is the car?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Jasmine, please look at your own paper. You need to do your math.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Excitedly shakes her braids and rubs her fingers together quickly in front of the ABC book) O the O says/ o/, octopus. the T says…

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: (Points to the math worksheet) You cannot read the ABC book right now. We have music next, so you need to do your math.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Grabs the ABC book again) No! Aaahh!

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time to complete your math worksheet. Please color the objects on the page in groups of four.

STUDENT: Let’s do some colors! What color is the apple? What color is the boy? What color is the car?

TUTOR: Jasmine, please look at your own paper. You need to do your math.

STUDENT: (Excitedly shakes her braids and rubs her fingers together quickly in front of the ABC book) O the O says/ o/, octopus. the T says…

TUTOR: (Points to the math worksheet) You cannot read the ABC book right now. We have music next, so you need to do your math.

STUDENT: (Grabs the ABC book again) No! Aaahh!

task.content: Complete a math worksheet back at their tables
task.learning_goal: Color the objects on the page in groups of 4

context.environment: Kindergarten class, at a round table
context.materials: Math worksheet, ABC book, favorite color crayon (purple)
context.social_setting: Inclusive classroom, sitting with a peer (Jeff) and a paraprofessional

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When the paraprofessional redirects Jasmine to the math worksheet by pointing, reminds her they have music next, and tells her she cannot read the ABC book right now
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Protests by grabbing the ABC book again and loudly saying 'no', protests by yelling 'aaahh', and occasionally protests by saying 'no' in a very high-pitched voice while working
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Appears to want to escape a task that she possibly considered boring, and to subsequently interact with Jeff

behavior_patterns.condition: When attempting to interact with a peer during or after completing her assigned task
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Employs familiar classroom scripts mimicking the teacher in form and intonation, excitedly shakes her braids, rubs her fingers together quickly in front of the book, waves her fingers in front of her eyes, and leans over the table waving her arms
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Interest in maintaining her interaction with Jeff is clear
related_quotes: What color is the apple? What color is the boy? What color is the car?
Write your name on the top
O the O says/ o/, octopus
